title: World Cup 2026 Awards: Mbappé Claims Record Golden Boot as Spain Sweep Individual Honours
excerpt: Kylian Mbappé became the first player to win back-to-back Golden Boots with 10 goals, while Spain's Rodri, Unaí Simón, and Pau Cubarsí claimed the Golden Ball, Golden Glove, and Best Young Player awards respectively.
body:
• France's Kylian Mbappé won the Golden Boot with 10 goals and four assists, becoming the first player in World Cup history to win back-to-back Golden Boots and overtaking Lionel Messi as the all-time World Cup leading scorer with 22 goals.
  • Spain captain Rodri took home the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player, orchestrating a midfield that produced six clean-sheet victories across eight matches.
  • Spain goalkeeper Unaí Simón won the Golden Glove with six clean sheets, while 18-year-old teammate Pau Cubarsí earned the Best Young Player Award.
  • Spain swept three of the four major individual awards, underscoring La Roja's dominance in a tournament where they conceded just one goal en route to the title.

The 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States crowned its individual award winners on Sunday, with Spain claiming three of the four major honours and France's Kylian Mbappé taking the most coveted individual prize — the Golden Boot — with a record-tying 10 goals.

Golden Boot: Kylian Mbappé (France) — 10 Goals, 4 Assists

Mbappé's 10-goal haul tied Gerd Müller's mark from the 1970 World Cup and made the 27-year-old the first player in tournament history to win consecutive Golden Boots. He claimed his first at Qatar 2022 with eight goals, despite France's defeat in the final.

The Real Madrid forward added a brace in France's 6-4 third-place defeat to England on July 18 in Miami to cement his lead. Across three World Cup campaigns, Mbappé has now scored 22 goals in 22 matches, overtaking Messi (21 goals in 33 matches) as the all-time leading World Cup scorer.

"Kylian Mbappé has become the first player in history to win TWO World Cup Golden Boots."

Messi, who opened with a hat-trick against Algeria and finished with eight goals and four assists, was kept scoreless in the final as Spain's defense shut him down. Other contenders included England's Jude Bellingham (seven goals, one assist), Norway's Erling Haaland (seven goals), and France's Ousmane Dembélé (six goals, two assists).

Golden Ball: Rodri (Spain)

Spain's captain Rodrigo Hernández Cascante, known universally as Rodri, was named the tournament's best player. The Manchester City midfielder anchored a Spanish side that set a record of 38 consecutive unbeaten matches in international play.

In the semifinal against France, Rodri won 11 duels — more than the entire French midfield combined — to propel Spain into the final. He joins an elite group as the 11th player in history to hold the World Cup, Champions League, and Ballon d'Or trophies simultaneously.

"We are a bit shocked right now, even myself. Now I'm like in a cloud."

— Rodri, Spain captain, on post-game broadcast

Golden Glove: Unaí Simón (Spain)

Spain's goalkeeper was a wall throughout the tournament, recording six clean sheets across eight matches. In the final, he was largely protected by a defense that limited Argentina to just one shot on target over 120 minutes. His performances anchored a Spanish backline that conceded only one goal in the entire competition — a record level of defensive solidity for a World Cup winner.

Best Young Player: Pau Cubarsí (Spain)

The 18-year-old Barcelona centre-back capped a breakthrough tournament with the Best Young Player Award. Cubarsí formed a formidable partnership with Aymeric Laporte at the heart of Spain's defense and was the target of Enzo Fernández's red-card challenge in the final. His composure beyond his years marked him as one of European football's most exciting defensive prospects.

Football's Global Reach

The awards underscored the depth of talent across continents, with individual brilliance from a Frenchman and collective excellence from Spain defining the tournament. For Indian football fans who followed the World Cup in record numbers, the performances of Cubarsí and Lamine Yamal — both teenagers — offered inspiration as India's own football development programmes seek to produce players capable of competing on the world stage through the All India Football Federation's grassroots initiatives.
